edits.inserted_text:
**[STU-RAS-180] PROVISIONAL LAYER-EFFECT AND ADVANCED-BLENDING REPRESENTATIONS (Operator decision D19,
2026-10-14).** Until the D5 Adobe oracle session decides Photoshop parity, Studio uses these
representations; each is the one the implementation carries, and each Photoshop-parity question
named below stays open under D5:

- (a) Knockout. The layer knockout state is the four-member enumeration of [STU-VEC-153]
  (`unknown`, `disabled`, `enabled`, `inherited`); Photoshop's shallow/deep knockout depth has no
  Studio field. PSD import maps `knko` 0 or absent to `disabled`, 1 to `enabled`, 2 to `enabled`
  with typed loss `knockout_depth_not_represented`, and any other value to `unknown` with typed loss
  `knockout_value_unknown`. `enabled` (and `inherited` resolving to `enabled`) lowers to a shallow
  knockout, which the renderer refuses with the typed error `plan_knockout_unsupported`; deep
  knockout is never emitted. Which PSD value means shallow or deep is open under D5.
- (b) Global Light storage. The document-level Global Light of [STU-RAS-158] is stored in the
  per-document sidecar record `hsk.studio.raster_records@1` (field `global_light`, absent by default;
  when present `angle` in -180..180 degrees and `altitude` in 0..90 degrees, both required, no
  default), because `StudioDocument` gains no fields. An effect with `use_global_light = true`
  takes the Global Light angle; if none is recorded the effect is refused with
  `effect_global_light_unresolved`. Only drop shadow and inner shadow currently read it; Global
  Light altitude is stored but not yet read by any effect.
- (c) Adjustment record identity. `hsk.studio.adjustment@1` has no record ID prefix of its own; an
  adjustment record is keyed by the `SLYR` id of the `adjustment` layer that hosts it (the layer's
  `PrimitiveReference` payload names `hsk.studio.adjustment@1` and its own layer id), one record
  per hosting layer in both directions.
- (d) Spread and choke unit. `spread` (drop shadow, outer glow) and `choke` (inner shadow, inner
  glow) are stored as a percent 0..100 of the effect `size`, as Photoshop stores them, and the
  renderer takes the fraction percent/100. This replaces the `pixels` unit that [STU-RAS-157]
  states for these fields. Drop-shadow spread model: the matte is grown hard by spread x size
  pixels, then blurred by size - spread x size, then offset by distance at the shadow angle.
- (e) Multi-instance order. Render order is list order within each placement class: drop shadow
  and outer glow render behind the layer content, every other effect kind over it; bottom to top
  the order is every behind-content instance in list order, then the content, then every
  over-content instance in list order. PSD single-instance slots and multi-instance lists merge in
  descriptor order with typed loss `effect_single_and_multi_slots_merged`.
- (f) Engineering maxima. The renderer accepts effect `size` up to 1000 px, shadow `distance` up to
  30000 px, at most 64 effect instances per layer and at most 4096 per render plan; beyond these it
  refuses with the typed limit errors (`effect_size_out_of_range`, `effect_distance_out_of_range`,
  `plan_effect_limit`/`effect_limit`; PSD import `effects_over_budget`). The stored effect stack
  admits at most 1024 instances. These are engineering bounds, not Photoshop limits.
- (g) Effect matte. The effect matte is derived from the layer's shape alpha: content alpha after
  the layer mask, before fill opacity; effects fade with effect opacity x layer opacity.
- (h) Clipping to an adjustment layer. An `adjustment` layer is not a clipping base: a layer whose
  clip base would be an adjustment layer is refused (`AdjustmentClipBase`; renderer
  `plan_adjustment_clip_base`). PSD import unclips such a layer and records the typed loss
  `clip_to_adjustment_not_supported`. Photoshop allows this clipping; parity is open under D5.
basis: START_LOG D19 entry (line beginning '- D19 (2026-10-11T05:57:08Z'), items (a)-(h)

edits.inserted_text:
**[STU-VEC-200] PROVISIONAL CLIP, MASK AND PATTERN-PAINT REPRESENTATIONS (Operator decision D19 (i),
2026-10-14).** [STU-VEC-053] is carried by the per-document sidecar record set
`hsk.studio.vector_records@1` (patterns, pattern paints, clips, masks, attachments; `StudioDocument`
and `StudioPaint` gain nothing) with these representations, each the one the implementation
carries; Adobe-application parity of each stays open under the D5 oracle session:

- Clip rule: `NONZERO` or `EVENODD` (the [STU-VEC-110] tokens); `NONE` is not a clip rule.
- Clip region: the vector geometry of the clip's source layer, which MUST carry a vector or group
  payload. A mask MAY carry a rectangular `region` outside which it is fully transparent.
- Units: every length is in the document unit; any other unit is refused. There is no
  object-bounding-box unit mode.
- Mask mode: the tokens `ALPHA`, `VECTOR`, `LUMINANCE` are stored with `mask_clip` and
  `invert_mask` (both default `false`); their computed semantics are not yet specified and nothing
  is computed from them. The use-as-mask marker is not stored: an attachment names each clipped or
  masked layer explicitly.
- Identity: pattern, clip and mask ids are set-local keys (ASCII alphanumerics, `_`, `-`, at most
  128 bytes) inside the record set; Accord defines no prefix for `hsk.studio.pattern@1` or for clips,
  and `SMSK` stays reserved for the raster `StudioMask`. Layer references are `SLYR`, style
  references `SSTY`.
- `overlap_order`: an opaque label; its members are not enumerated.
- Pattern placement: either the parametric transform of [STU-COL-196] or, as a Folio addition, an
  affine `matrix` `[a, b, c, d, e, f]` (point = [a c e; b d f] x [x y 1], pattern space to the
  filled object's space) that MUST be finite and invertible.
- PAINT-row binding: a pattern paint binds to a PAINT style by `(style_id, row)` where `row` is the
  index into the style's rows (fill or stroke); at most one binding per pair; the row MUST exist.
  Rows carry no id, so reordering rows MUST rewrite the bindings.
- Reference cycles are refused.

edits.inserted_text: [STU-IO-191] NATIVE-FIRST OPEN AND CONVERT (Operator instruction 2026-10-14). The Studio native container of [STU-IO-001] (`.handshake`) is Studio's primary document format; every [STU-IO-006] row is an interchange format around it. For rows 1 (`.psd`), 2 (`.psb`), 3 (`.tif`/`.tiff`), 13 (proprietary camera raw) and 14 (`.dng`) Studio MUST offer both: (a) open directly, one open command that runs the row's importer and presents the result as a native document; and (b) convert to native, writing that imported document as a native container. Both are one shared flow (importer, then native document, then container) that carries the import loss receipt and provenance and preserves the original source per [STU-IO-001] and [STU-IO-005]. PDF is a required compatibility surface: a native document MUST be exportable to PDF (rows 20, 26, 27) and a PDF MUST be importable into a native document (row 20). This clause adds no direction token and changes no row; every claim stays gated by [STU-IO-004].

OPEN for the spec owner: 'primary document format' must be reconciled with STU-IO-001 'The container is import/export/recovery transport; integrated durable and collaborative authority remains SurrealDB/EventLedger/CRDT'. The proposal treats .handshake as the primary user-facing open/save format while Studio is standalone, and does not change durable authority once integrated.
Row 13 (camera raw) has no export direction; the instruction does not require one, so none is proposed.
Adding STU-IO-191 may change the interoperability microtask count (STU-IO-172 / v02.207 amendment counting); reconcile when applying.
